notes: Deal choice. Trust names and CIKs come from the EDGAR quarterly ABS-EE index lists for 2026 Q3/Q4 saved earlier in Veritas_Hackathon_2026_Finance_Ideas/feature_hunt/lanes/3_data/sec/; filing dates from each trust's data.sec.gov submissions JSON. Brief windows: Jan-Jun 2024 -> 2024-A (pool ABS-EE 2024-01-16; 2024-B, filed 2024-04-16, is also in the window and was not used); Jan-Jun 2025 -> 2025-A (2025-01-14); Oct 2025-Feb 28 2026 -> 2026-A (2026-01-06), the latest Toyota pool filing in that window: 2026-B's first ABS-EE is dated 2026-04-07 (its submissions JSON was checked). All three are Toyota Auto Receivables Owner Trusts (prime retail loans; no lease trust).

Each deal's pool ABS-EE filings are the trust's first ABS-EE, filed after an ABS-15G and before the 424H and 424B5. Toyota files one pool file per deal size offered: 'sp' and 'lp' for 2024-A and 2025-A, 'sp', 'mp' and 'lp' for 2026-A. In all three deals the 'lp' file's row count equals the 424B5 'Number of Receivables' exactly (71,726; 69,132; 65,867). The sp/mp files were not downloaded. Each downloaded file's size equals the size in EDGAR's index.json.

Cutoff balance check. For 2024-A and 2025-A the sum of reportingPeriodBeginningLoanBalanceAmount equals the 424B5 Total Principal Balance to the cent ($1,908,468,799.65; $1,977,161,496.74); for 2026-A the sum of reportingPeriodActualEndBalanceAmount does ($1,995,353,675.63). Weighted by that column, the file reproduces the 424B5 summary: weighted APR 5.3726% / 6.0039% / 5.6771% (424B5 5.37% / 6.00% / 5.68%), weighted FICO 767.03 / 769.42 / 770.77 (424B5 767 / 769 / 771), share of new_used_code '1' 84.18% / 91.00% / 87.96% (424B5 'New vehicles' 84.18% / 91.00% / 87.96%). This confirms apr_pct's scale and that new_used_code '1' = New, '2' = Used.

subvented repeats inside one loan: the spec allows several <subvented> elements (maxOccurs unbounded) and Toyota writes both '1' (rate subvention) and '2' (cash rebate) on 4,703 / 4,487 / 3,929 loans. Those loans are stored as '1,2' (all values, file order, joined by a comma). Note for the main session: parse_carmax.py builds a dict per loan, so a parser copied from it unchanged keeps only the last repeated value ('2'); this parser records every repeated tag in stats_<deal>.json (only subvented and, for a few loans, modificationTypeCode repeat).

Credit scores: obligorCreditScoreType is 'FICO Score 8 Auto' for every loan and every score is numeric (100%). Range 620-900 in all three deals, the same as the 424B5 'Range of FICO scores 620 - 900'; medians 772 / 775 / 776. Scores above 850 (8,362 / 8,793 / 8,954 rows) are normal on the FICO Auto 8 scale (250-900); none are outside 250-900.

Pools are seasoned: origination months 2018-02..2023-07 (cutoff 2023-12), 2019-02..2024-07 (cutoff 2024-12), 2020-02..2025-07 (cutoff 2025-11). Share originated 12 or more months before the cutoff month: 51.3% / 50.9% / 40.4%. The newest loans are about five months older than the cutoff. No loan was originated after 2026-01.
apr_pct is exactly 0 for 1,159 / 934 / 686 loans (the 424B5 range of APRs starts at 0.00%); kept as written. Maximum 21.33 / 23.22 / 23.29, equal to the 424B5 ranges.

Other codes as written: interest_rate_type_code '1' (fixed) for every loan; vehicle_value_source_code '1' (invoice price) for exactly the new-vehicle loans, '3' (Kelley Blue Book) or '98' (other) for used ones; vehicle_type_code 1/2/3 (car/truck/SUV); income_verification_code 2/3; employment_verification_code 2/3; co_obligor and state present for every loan. paymentToIncomePercentage is a fraction (median 0.0757), so pti_pct = value x 100 as in CONTRACT; none missing. vehicle_make and vehicle_model carry trailing spaces in the file and are stripped, as parse_carmax.py does.

Downloads: Python requests with the sec.gov User-Agent from CLAUDE.md passed in the SEC_UA environment variable (not stored in any file), one request at a time, at least 1.1 s apart, no retries; every request is logged in data/raw/toyota/sec_requests.log (git-ignored).
